## 1. Overall assessment

**Your detailed career evidence is generally stronger than the language used to summarize it.**

The résumé family contains substantial accounts of customer remediation, analytical development, executive decisions, research, validation, and delivery. The weakness emerges when those accounts are compressed into labels such as “analytical-system governance,” “DFAST decision-tree segmentation,” or an isolated furnishing-volume statistic. The current Senior profile illustrates that compression directly. fileciteturn9file0L15-L23

That means the right solution is not to make the résumé less technical or replace accomplishments with generic leadership prose. It is to **restore the relationship between the assignment, your contribution, the result or decision, and the supporting technical evidence.**

I reviewed all three current R2 baselines and the private brief completely: **11 pages and 311 nonempty body/table-cell paragraphs**, including headings and administrative text. The diagnostic identifies **42 substantive editorial or interpretation findings**. These are not 42 newly discovered false career facts; they include scope risks, hierarchy problems, duplication, weak labels, and reuse-control defects.

| **Senior — two pages** | The opening is overloaded, and some of the strongest professional work is obscured by methods, controls, and compressed project fragments. | Rebuild the opening hierarchy; lead Wells Fargo with CPI customer-remediation work; simplify repeated capability/toolkit material. |
| **Enterprise — three pages** | Contains some of the best developed project narratives, but combines them with dense inventories and repeated governance-oriented framing. | Preserve the strong stories; sharpen the mandate and decision/delivery emphasis; reduce duplication. |

## 2. The most important findings beyond the issues we already discussed

### The private brief is a source of recurring narrative drift

This is the most consequential finding.

The brief contains sound instructions to explain the business problem before architecture or metrics. But it also directs future writers to lead with CPI analytical-system ownership and, for modeling-oriented letters, “DFAST decision-tree segmentation” and a method list. Those instructions are inconsistent with the hierarchy we have now established. fileciteturn9file3L740-L747 fileciteturn9file3L754-L761

**Editing the résumé profiles alone would leave instructions that can generate the same problems again.**

I recommend separating the private brief’s functions: career identity, employer mandates, contextualized project stories, factual definitions, and rules for using those facts. A definition such as “100M+ means account-month actions” is necessary, but it does not prevent that true figure from being used in the wrong place.

### “CPI model-like production” should be removed

The Credit Risk résumé currently uses this accomplishment heading:

> “CPI model-like production, business intelligence, and sustained assurance…”

The paragraph beneath it describes recalculation tools, insurance evidence, customer redress, recurring production, reporting, and assurance. Those are substantive accomplishments in their own right. “Model-like” adds an unnecessary analogy and can suggest a formal model classification that the wording does not establish. fileciteturn9file2L427-L432

**The specialist résumé should explain why your remediation calculations and validation experience matter—not rename the work to make it sound more model-oriented.**

### “Target Operating Model ownership” needs an ownership qualifier

Enterprise and Credit Risk use:

> “Executive decision leadership and Target Operating Model ownership…”

The body supports ownership of analytical workstreams and analytical artifacts **under** the remediation operating model. The heading can be read as ownership of the complete operating model. fileciteturn9file1L187-L192 fileciteturn9file2L421-L426

I recommend retaining the strength of the contribution while identifying the actual ownership: analytical leadership, decisions, and execution under the Remediation Target Operating Model.

### The promotion sentence creates an avoidable chronology implication

Senior says you were promoted “after leading” a collection of work that includes CPI responsibilities through 2025. The dated role history places the promotion in June 2022. This is an ambiguity in sentence construction—not a finding that the promotion date is wrong. fileciteturn9file0L18-L20 fileciteturn9file0L39-L41

The remedy is simple: separate the promotion fact from the full multiyear accomplishment record. Do not imply that promotion followed the completed 2018–2025 period or invent a particular cause.

Relatedly, “seven years” should describe **your CPI analytical work**, not the legal duration of the remediation. Your private brief already makes that distinction explicitly. fileciteturn9file3L734-L735

### The $1B+ measure needs a clearer grammatical home

In Credit Risk, the placement of “exceeding $1B in exposure and customer impact” after the furnishing-control wording can make the amount appear to describe those controls. The accepted private positioning attaches it to the broader Consumer Auto programs. fileciteturn9file2L353-L356 fileciteturn9file3L544-L546

I recommend placing the measure immediately beside **Consumer Auto programs**. It should not resemble furnishing-history volume, personal P&L, or a realized-savings claim.

### The private 15+ example list is internally inconsistent

The brief describes **15+ additional Consumer Auto remediations**, but its later example list includes CPI within the 15+ workstreams. fileciteturn9file3L589-L591 fileciteturn9file3L605-L608

I recommend aligning the example list with the controlling “15+ additional” formulation, keeping CPI separately described, and preserving the **10+ advised/peer-reviewed efforts as a separate measure**. This does not require inventing or recalculating a combined total.

## 4. Recommended executive-profile architecture

I recommend keeping the existing professional identities and differentiating the three profiles through **emphasis**, not through different underlying career claims.

**Senior:** senior analytical identity → hands-on ownership → principal Wells Fargo evidence → OCC breadth → current independent capability.

**Enterprise:** business requirements and analytical products → executive decisions and cross-functional delivery → sustained operation and review → institutional breadth → business-facing independent applications.

**Credit Risk:** economist/examination partnership → analytical development, methods, and validation → Wells Fargo production-remediation discipline → current synthetic credit-strategy and statistical work.

The current top capability boxes should become much shorter navigation aids. They should not repeat the profile and then repeat the bottom toolkit again. The present boxes contain precisely the method/control shorthand that is competing with your actual experience. fileciteturn9file0L24-L37 fileciteturn9file1L166-L175 fileciteturn9file2L359-L371

> Senior analytics and applied data science leader with 16+ years across Wells Fargo, the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency, and the U.S. Census Bureau, including 12 years in regulated credit-risk analytics. Combines hands-on SAS, SQL, and Python with analytical ownership from source data and methodology through business decisions, implementation, and validation. At Wells Fargo, led analytics for the Collateral Protection Insurance (CPI) customer remediation and 15+ additional Consumer Auto remediations within programs exceeding $1B in exposure and customer impact; promoted to Senior Lead Analytics Consultant at the Executive Director level. Earlier OCC work spanned credit research, bank examination and stress-testing analytics, CECL, and independent validation. Current independent work uses synthetic data to demonstrate configurable credit-strategy testing, merchant-financing analytics, Power BI applications, and Python time-to-event analysis.

This retains your accepted seniority, credit foundation, technical identity, program scope, and title distinction while removing the furnishing-statistic and DFAST-technique fragments. The professional foundation and tool classifications are supported by the private brief. fileciteturn9file3L541-L559

The distinction here is **analytical development carried through decisions and sustained delivery**, rather than a larger collection of governance terms. That emphasis comes from the detailed professional record. fileciteturn9file3L589-L611 fileciteturn9file1L231-L279

## 6. The highest-impact project-level changes

### CPI: put customer remediation before the machinery

**Current lead-in:**

> “CPI recalculation, explainability, and sustained assurance…”

The underlying paragraph has good technical evidence, but the label does not immediately communicate customer remediation. fileciteturn9file0L57-L60

**Proposed:**

> **CPI customer-remediation analytics and delivery (2018–2025):** Designed and owned Direct and Indirect Auto recalculation tools and proof-of-insurance intake/QA to apply coverage adjustments, account-level redress, time-value-of-money relief, and prior-payment netting. Operated recurring analytical production, integrated manual-review results, and maintained the reporting, controls, and evidence needed for customer support and Audit/regulatory review.

The approximately 30-program suite and narrowly scoped proof-of-insurance Audit result remain available in the detailed version and private record. They are not being erased; they simply do not all need to compete inside every compressed version.

### DFAST: describe the assignment, then the examples

The current R2 body correctly removes the Auto restriction, but still moves directly from the DFAST heading into the specific data/projection/segmentation example. fileciteturn9file0L91-L93

**Proposed:**

> **DFAST examination and stress-testing analytics:** Provided analytical support to OCC economists across the DFAST review process as credit-portfolio questions arose. Analyzed bank-provided data and nine-quarter stress projections, tested portfolio segmentation using decision trees, and compared aggregate and segment-level results to identify issues for further economist and examination-team review.

This incorporates your broader process clarification without claiming that you personally handled every institutional schedule, portfolio, or stage of DFAST.

### Favorable-state persistence: preserve the complete project logic

The Senior bullet currently begins with consolidation and the 500+/100M+ figures; the overwrite-prevention purpose appears later. Enterprise already provides a more complete account. fileciteturn9file0L69-L73 fileciteturn9file1L205-L211

**Proposed:**

Standardized 500+ archived submission files representing 100M+ account-month actions, aligned proposed updates with prior activity, and supported targeted correction. Defended a unified customer-relief approach while preserving reporting that distinguished remediation-caused from furnishing-caused overwrites.

This illustrates the required context, **not a requirement that Senior retain every project number**. The detailed version/private record retains the 20M+ evaluation, “most required no update,” and separate UAT distinctions.

The enterprise credit-governance significance remains. What disappears is the isolated scale fragment pretending to explain it.

### Decision leadership: lead with judgment, not deck handling

The current language begins “Authored, reviewed, edited, and presented Decision Forum decks.” The remainder contains the stronger contribution. fileciteturn9file0L53-L56

**Proposed:**

> **Remediation decision leadership:** Framed customer-impact issues, evaluated feasible treatment alternatives, and presented recommendations to cross-functional Decision Forums. Supplied the supporting analytics, answered challenge, and ensured approved decisions and material changes were documented and reflected in analytical execution, while reviewing partner-owned artifacts for alignment.

This strengthens the narrative without adding final approval authority or claiming ownership of other functions’ artifacts.

## 7. Recommended substantive treatment of the remaining sections

### Wells Fargo

I recommend leading each Wells section with **CPI financial-remediation analytics and delivery**, followed by **CPI credit-reporting correction**. Broader remediation/decision leadership follows, then selected key projects and supporting delivery/assurance evidence.

The catch-all standards/tax/mentoring/aged-review bullet should be separated or selectively condensed. Those are distinct contributions; combining them merely to save a bullet weakens each. The private brief already records them separately. fileciteturn9file3L637-L644

### OCC

The Auto research should begin with the **loan-term, delinquency-risk, and customer-pricing question**, then explain your engineering, validation, scale, and economist-led methods.

CECL should begin with **developing and testing lifetime-PD approaches for economists**, then explain vendor/data fitness, acquisition advice, assumptions, sensitivities, and presentations.

Cross-bank risk-rating comparison and cross-product delinquency sequencing should retain their purpose and remain distinguishable. They should not be unexplained add-ons to a generic validation bullet. The detailed Enterprise version contains the necessary distinction. fileciteturn9file1L235-L251

The changes should be smaller. Combine the ACES pipeline and its analyst/management purpose more clearly; retain day-to-day production leadership. Keep ARTS’s on-demand SAS-to-Excel/VBA workflow distinct. Consolidate repeated statistical-control lists rather than removing the statistical foundation. fileciteturn9file1L267-L279
